lesson.title: How's your family?
lesson.scenario: Fattoush asks Knafeh about his family. Knafeh returns the interest by asking about Fattoush’s mother. Share only the detail the scene gives you.

steps.instruction: Ask Knafeh about his family, rather than about your own.

answers.rationale: Ahli refers to the speaker’s family instead of Knafeh’s.
Ahlak means Knafeh’s family when he is the listener.
This asks about Knafeh himself, not his family.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ahlak means Knafeh’s family when he is the listener.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: The ending should mean “your” to Knafeh.

steps.instruction: Knafeh says the family members are well. Respond as Knafeh.

answers.rationale: This refers to one woman, not the family group.
This updates only Knafeh’s condition.
Mnīḥīn refers to the family members as a group.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Mnīḥīn refers to the family members as a group.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Answer about the group of people.

steps.instruction: Follow up specifically about Knafeh’s sister.

answers.meaning: And your sister, how is she? (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: Naming the sister gives kīfha a clear referent.
This repeats the general family question instead of following up about his sister.
This asks Fattoush about her mother; both the listener and relative change.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Naming the sister gives kīfha a clear referent.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Name the sister before asking how she is.

steps.instruction: The sister is well but has much work. Give that update.

prompt.meaning: And your sister, how is she? (to Knafeh)

answers.meaning: She’s well. Today she’s at home.
answers.rationale: Being home today is a different detail; it does not express the sister’s workload.

answers.meaning: I have a lot of work.
answers.rationale: This changes the person from the sister to the speaker.

answers.meaning: She’s well, but she has a lot of work.
answers.rationale: Both the positive condition and the work detail match the scenario.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Both the positive condition and the work detail match the scenario.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: The work belongs to her: ʿindha.

steps.instruction: Fattoush has just mentioned her mother. Ask a short follow-up about the mother.

answers.rationale: This asks about Fattoush rather than her mother.
Kīfha refers back to the mother Fattoush has just named.

answers.meaning: What did you do today? (to Fattoush)
answers.rationale: This asks broadly about Fattoush’s activities instead of following up on her mother.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Kīfha refers back to the mother Fattoush has just named.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: The short ending should refer to “her.”

steps.instruction: Knafeh wants to ask Fattoush about her family. Choose the address to Fattoush.

answers.rationale: Ahlik is the selected feminine address; Arabic script alone may not show the short-vowel difference.
Ahlak is addressed to Knafeh, not Fattoush.
This asks about the speaker’s own family.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ahlik is the selected feminine address; Arabic script alone may not show the short-vowel difference.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 1: today Fattoush’s mother is well and at home. Reply as Fattoush.

answers.meaning: She’s well, but she has a lot of work.
answers.rationale: This introduces a heavy workload, which the new scene does not give.
This answers about several people, not the mother.

answers.meaning: She’s well. Today she’s at home.
answers.rationale: This gives the mother’s condition and today’s location without inventing extra detail.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This gives the mother’s condition and today’s location without inventing extra detail.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Keep the referent singular and the detail about home.

steps.instruction: Closing exchange, part 2: agree to the proposed visit tomorrow.

answers.rationale: This reports a past visit today; it does not agree to tomorrow’s visit.
This agrees to the future shared visit and keeps the same person and day.
This declines rather than accepting the invitation.

evaluation.correctExplanation: This agrees to the future shared visit and keeps the same person and day.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: This is a possible expression, but it does not meet the request in this situation.
evaluation.retryHint: Accept the invitation and preserve tomorrow.

lesson.unitTitle: Everyday conversations with someone you love

introduction.goal: Ask about someone’s family, share a short update, and ask a relevant follow-up.

line.meaning: And your sister, how is she? (to Knafeh)

line.arabic: منيحة، بس عندها شغل كتير. وكيف أمك؟
line.arabizi: Mnīḥa, bass ʿindha shughl ktīr. W-kīf immik?
line.meaning: She’s well, but she has a lot of work. And how’s your mother?
She’s well. Today she’s at home.
Good! Shall we visit her tomorrow?

expressions.meaning: And your sister, how is she? (to Knafeh)
She’s well, but she has a lot of work.

introduction.usageNote: Keep track of the person you address and the person you describe. Ahlak or ahlik asks about your listener’s family; ahli means my family. After the mother or sister is mentioned, kīfha asks about her.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target. This dialogue names the people before using “her.” Ahlak/ukhtak address Knafeh; ahlik/ukhtik address Fattoush. Immi is “my mother”; immik here is “your mother” when speaking to Fattoush. These are contextual choices, not the only Palestinian vowel variants. Transliteration: ā/ī/ū and ē/ō mark long vowels; ʿ = ع, ḥ = ح, ʾ = glottal stop, sh = ش, kh = خ, gh = غ. Doubled letters are held longer. Jordanian alternatives are not introduced in this unit.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings yet. This six-turn transcript is the recording script: Fattoush uses feminine self-description; Knafeh uses masculine self-description. Read each speaker’s turns in order, then the practice prompts and answer options as separate clips. Retain the marked address distinctions. A Palestinian speaker and owner must check wording/pronunciation before assets are labeled reviewed. Optional device speech is a variable browser preview, not a dialect model.

teachingCards.title: Ask about their family
teachingCards.note: Ahlak means your family when speaking to Knafeh; ahli means my family. Listen to the ending and keep transliteration handy.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Fattoush. Ask Knafeh how his family is.

teachingCards.title: Answer about people together
teachingCards.note: Mnīḥīn describes the family members as people. It differs from mnīḥa for the mother or sister.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Tell Fattoush your family members are well and thank her.

teachingCards.title: Follow up about his sister

phrase.meaning: And your sister, how is she? (to Knafeh)

teachingCards.note: Ukhtak is your sister when addressing Knafeh. Kīfha then refers to that sister, not to Knafeh.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Fattoush. Follow up specifically about Knafeh’s sister.

teachingCards.title: Give a small update

phrase.meaning: She’s well, but she has a lot of work.

teachingCards.note: Start with the sister’s condition. Bass introduces a contrast; ʿindha shughl says she has work, and ktīr gives the amount.
teachingCards.recallCue: Knafeh’s sister is well but has a lot of work. Give her update.

teachingCards.title: Turn the family question back
teachingCards.note: Ahlik addresses Fattoush. It looks the same as ahlak in this unvowelled spelling, so the transliteration shows the spoken difference.
teachingCards.recallCue: You are Knafeh. Ask Fattoush how her family is.

teachingCards.title: Agree to a visit
teachingCards.note: Bukra sets the plan in tomorrow. In nzūrha, the ending -ha points back to Fattoush’s mother; you are agreeing to visit her together.
teachingCards.recallCue: Fattoush’s mother is at home. Agree to visit her together tomorrow.
